title: Cutaneous Lymphoma Classification (WHO-EORTC 2018)
subtitle: Cutaneous T-cell and NK-cell lymphomas — with B-cell overview

children.name: Mycosis Fungoides (MF) and Variants
children.detail: Classic MF: patch, plaque, tumor progression. CD3+, CD4+, CD7 loss common. Indolent clinical course in early stages.

children.name: Classic Mycosis Fungoides
children.detail: Patch-plaque-tumor progression with epidermotropism and Pautrier microabscesses. Indolent; most patients remain in early stage.

children.name: Folliculotropic MF
children.detail: Follicular tropism with papules, cysts, comedones; preferential head/neck involvement; often worse prognosis than classic MF due to reduced skin-directed therapy penetration.

children.name: Pagetoid Reticulosis (Woringer-Kolopp)
children.detail: Solitary or localized psoriasiform plaque with marked intraepidermal proliferation of neoplastic T-cells. Excellent prognosis; localized radiation is curative.

children.name: Granulomatous Slack Skin
children.detail: Rare variant: granulomatous destruction of elastic fibers causing pendulous skin in flexural areas. Slow progression; associated with Hodgkin lymphoma in ~30%.

children.name: Sézary Syndrome (SS)
children.detail: Triad: erythroderma, lymphadenopathy, and Sézary cells in blood (>1000/mcL or B2 criteria). CD4+, CD7-, CD26- phenotype. Prognosis poor with median OS 2-5 years. ECP is cornerstone of treatment.

children.name: Lymphomatoid Papulosis (LyP)
children.detail: Recurrent, self-healing papulonodular eruption with histologic features of malignancy. Five subtypes (A-F). CD30+ in most subtypes. Benign clinical behavior despite alarming histology; watch-and-wait for mild disease. Associated with risk of secondary lymphoma (~15%).

children.name: Primary Cutaneous Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma (pcALCL)
children.detail: Solitary or grouped tumors/nodules; CD30+ (>75% of cells). ALK-negative (distinguishes from systemic ALCL). Excellent prognosis with 5-year OS >85%. Excision or local radiation for solitary lesions; brentuximab vedotin or methotrexate for multifocal disease.

children.name: Subcutaneous Panniculitis-like T-Cell Lymphoma (SPTCL)
children.detail: Alpha-beta T-cell phenotype (CD3+, CD8+, CD4-, CD56-); subcutaneous fat involvement mimicking panniculitis. Indolent course unless hemophagocytic syndrome develops. Cyclosporine or bexarotene; CHOP for aggressive disease.

children.name: Extranodal NK/T-Cell Lymphoma, Nasal Type
children.detail: EBV-positive; CD56+, cytotoxic markers (TIA-1, granzyme B); angiocentric invasion with necrosis. Nasal and upper aerodigestive tract involvement common. Highly aggressive; L-asparaginase-based regimens (SMILE, AspaMetDex) are first-line.

children.name: Primary Cutaneous Peripheral T-Cell Lymphomas (Rare Subtypes)
Primary Cutaneous Gamma-Delta T-Cell Lymphoma
children.detail: Gamma-delta TCR phenotype; CD3+, CD4-, CD8- (double-negative). Aggressive; involves dermis and subcutis. Poor prognosis; allogeneic SCT considered.

children.name: Primary Cutaneous CD8+ Aggressive Epidermotropic Cytotoxic T-Cell Lymphoma
children.detail: Rapidly progressive papulonodules with ulceration and necrosis. CD3+, CD8+, TIA-1+. Very poor prognosis; median OS <2 years.

children.name: Primary Cutaneous Peripheral T-Cell Lymphoma, NOS
children.detail: Diagnosis of exclusion after ruling out other defined entities. Heterogeneous; generally poor prognosis.

children.name: Primary Cutaneous Follicle Center Lymphoma (PCFCL)
children.detail: Most common CBCL. CD20+, BCL-6+, BCL-2 typically negative (unlike nodal FCL). Head, neck, trunk. Excellent prognosis; local radiation curative in most cases.

children.name: Primary Cutaneous Marginal Zone Lymphoma (PCMZL)
children.detail: CD20+, CD79a+, BCL-2+; indolent. Arms, trunk. Association with Borrelia burgdorferi in Europe. Excellent prognosis; localized treatment sufficient.

children.name: Primary Cutaneous Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma, Leg Type
children.detail: CD20+, BCL-2+, MYC+; aggressive. Predominantly on lower legs of elderly women. Poor prognosis; R-CHOP is standard treatment.

citations.quote: Willemze R et al. The 2018 update of the WHO-EORTC classification for primary cutaneous lymphomas. Blood. 2019;133(16):1703-1714.
